```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status: EXPLORATORY throughout.** Nothing here is in the pre-specified confirmatory set, and every
p-value and CI is unadjusted. Section headers carry the label so it cannot be lost.

**Question.** What does wheat inoculation do to the *competitive balance* between wheat and fava in
the 30 intercrop pots, and does it change across drought? Fava suppression (Fig. 3, section R5)
showed the fava side. This asks whether wheat gains when fava is suppressed, and whether the pot as
a whole gains or loses.

**Conventions.** The randomized `Inoc` factor is the predictor (colonization is a plant response, not
a treatment). Every model is `Inoc * Water`, fitted **once** on all 30 intercrop pots and conditioned
within with `emmeans`; no subset models. Effects are `Inoc - Strl` with 95% CIs, n = 5 per cell.
Wheat biomass here is the **pot total** for the 6 wheat plants (`W_NPP`), not per plant.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(car)
library(nlme)

inter <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>% filter(Poly == "Inter") %>%
  mutate(wheat = W_NPP, fava = Fava_g, pot = Pot_NPP_g,
         log_fava = log(fava), log_wheat = log(wheat), log_pot = log(pot),
         log_ratio = log(wheat / fava))
stopifnot(nrow(inter) == 30, all(table(inter$Inoc, inter$Water) == 5),
          identical(levels(inter$Inoc), c("Inoc", "Strl")),
          all(inter$fava > 0), all(inter$wheat > 0),
          isTRUE(all.equal(inter$fava, inter$fava_npp)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(inter$pot, inter$wheat + inter$fava, tolerance = 1e-4)))  # pot = wheat + fava
```

# 1. Verification of the raw-mean table (descriptive)

Inoculated minus sterile, mean per pot, in grams. This checks the table in the prompt against the data.

```{r verify}
means <- inter %>% group_by(Water, Inoc) %>%
  summarise(fava = mean(fava), wheat = mean(wheat), pot = mean(pot), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Inoc, values_from = c(fava, wheat, pot)) %>%
  transmute(Water,
            d_fava = fava_Inoc - fava_Strl, d_wheat = wheat_Inoc - wheat_Strl,
            d_pot = pot_Inoc - pot_Strl, pot_pct = (pot_Inoc / pot_Strl - 1) * 100)

claimed <- tibble(Water = factor(c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe"), levels(inter$Water)),
                  c_fava = c(-6.12, -5.36, -0.44), c_wheat = c(-1.38, 4.90, 1.38), c_pot = c(-7.50, -0.46, 0.94))
chk <- left_join(means, claimed, by = "Water")
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$d_fava - chk$c_fava), abs(chk$d_wheat - chk$c_wheat), abs(chk$d_pot - chk$c_pot)) < 0.006)
knitr::kable(means %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))),
             col.names = c("Water", "Δ fava (g)", "Δ wheat (g)", "Δ total pot (g)", "Δ total pot (%)"),
             caption = "Raw cell-mean differences (Inoc - Strl), grams per pot. All values match the prompt's table; control total = -20%.")
```

All nine numbers and the −20% match. The raw means are correct; section 2 asks how well the data
back them up.

# 2. EXPLORATORY: models

## 2a. Variance check

Levene's test across the six cells for each response; a variance structure is used only if it is
violated (p < 0.05). AIC for alternatives is shown as a sensitivity check.

```{r variance}
resp <- tribble(~var,         ~label,
                "log_fava",   "log(fava)",
                "log_wheat",  "log(wheat, pot total)",
                "log_pot",    "log(total pot)",
                "log_ratio",  "log(wheat : fava)")
cell <- interaction(inter$Inoc, inter$Water)
inter$cell <- cell

fit_gls <- function(y, w = NULL) {
  f <- reformulate("Inoc * Water", y)
  eval(bquote(gls(.(f), weights = .(w), data = inter, method = "REML")))
}
vtab <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(resp)), function(i) {
  y <- resp$var[i]
  tibble(response = resp$label[i],
         `Levene, 6 cells (p)` = car::leveneTest(inter[[y]], cell, center = median)[1, "Pr(>F)"],
         AIC_equal = AIC(fit_gls(y)),
         `AIC varIdent(~1|Inoc)` = AIC(fit_gls(y, varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Inoc))),
         `AIC varIdent(~1|Water)` = AIC(fit_gls(y, varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Water))),
         `AIC varIdent(~1|cell)` = AIC(fit_gls(y, varIdent(form = ~ 1 | cell))))
})
knitr::kable(vtab %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))),
             caption = "Variance homogeneity (Levene) and AIC for alternative variance structures")
```

Levene's test is not violated for any response (all p > 0.4), so the primary models use equal
variance. The AIC differences are small and mostly favor nothing decisively (the one lower AIC for
fava under six free variances is estimated from five pots each); the effect of the best-fitting
alternative on the key estimates is checked in 2d.

## 2b. Effects, per water level

```{r effects}
get_eff <- function(var, label, scale = c("log", "identity")) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  m <- lm(reformulate("Inoc * Water", var), data = inter)
  p_iw <- car::Anova(m, type = 2)["Inoc:Water", "Pr(>F)"]
  s <- emmeans(m, ~ Inoc | Water) %>% contrast("pairwise", by = "Water", adjust = "none") %>%
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>% as.data.frame()
  stopifnot(all(s$contrast == "Inoc - Strl"))
  tibble(response = label, Water = factor(s$Water, levels(inter$Water)),
         est = s$estimate, lo = s$lower.CL, hi = s$upper.CL, p = s$p.value, p_interaction = p_iw,
         scale = scale)
}
log_eff <- bind_rows(
  get_eff("log_fava",  "Fava biomass",            "log"),
  get_eff("log_wheat", "Wheat biomass (pot total)", "log"),
  get_eff("log_pot",   "Total pot biomass",        "log"),
  get_eff("log_ratio", "Wheat : fava ratio",       "log")) %>%
  mutate(fold = exp(est), fold_lo = exp(lo), fold_hi = exp(hi),
         pct = (fold - 1) * 100, pct_lo = (fold_lo - 1) * 100, pct_hi = (fold_hi - 1) * 100)

gram_eff <- bind_rows(
  get_eff("fava", "Fava biomass",            "identity"),
  get_eff("wheat", "Wheat biomass (pot total)", "identity"),
  get_eff("pot",  "Total pot biomass",        "identity"))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 1e-4, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p, 2)))
knitr::kable(log_eff %>% filter(response != "Wheat : fava ratio") %>%
               transmute(response, Water, `% change` = round(pct, 1),
                         `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", pct_lo, pct_hi), p = fmt_p(p),
                         `Inoc x Water p` = fmt_p(p_interaction)),
             caption = "EXPLORATORY - Inoc - Strl effect on each biomass, % change (log-scale models; unadjusted 95% CI)")

knitr::kable(log_eff %>% filter(response == "Wheat : fava ratio") %>%
               transmute(Water, `fold-change in wheat:fava ratio` = round(fold, 2),
                         `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", fold_lo, fold_hi), p = fmt_p(p),
                         `Inoc x Water p` = fmt_p(p_interaction)),
             caption = "EXPLORATORY - competitive balance: fold-change in the wheat:fava ratio with inoculation (1 = no change)")

knitr::kable(gram_eff %>% transmute(response, Water, `difference (g per pot)` = round(est, 2),
                                    `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lo, hi), p = fmt_p(p)),
             caption = "EXPLORATORY - the same contrasts in grams per pot (identity-scale models); this is the scale a stacked-bar panel would show")
```

## 2c. Why the log ratio, and what it can and cannot say

The percentage of the pot that is fava (`Pot_pcent_fava`) conflates "fava shrank" with "wheat grew"
and cannot tell them apart. The log wheat:fava ratio is symmetric (a 2x change up or down has the
same magnitude) and additive, so a fold-change with a CI is interpretable. Its limitation is that
it is **mechanically driven by whichever component moves most**: here fava biomass moves by about
72-74% with a tight CI while wheat biomass is very noisy, so the ratio shift is almost entirely a
fava effect. A rising ratio does **not** mean wheat gained.

## 2d. Sensitivity of the key estimates to the variance structure

```{r sensitivity}
sens_eff <- function(var, label) {
  g <- fit_gls(var, varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Inoc))
  e <- emmeans(g, ~ Inoc | Water, data = inter) %>% contrast("pairwise", by = "Water", adjust = "none") %>%
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>% as.data.frame()
  tibble(response = label, Water = factor(e$Water, levels(inter$Water)),
         pct_alt = (exp(e$estimate) - 1) * 100, lo_alt = (exp(e$lower.CL) - 1) * 100,
         hi_alt = (exp(e$upper.CL) - 1) * 100)
}
alt <- bind_rows(sens_eff("log_fava", "Fava biomass"), sens_eff("log_wheat", "Wheat biomass (pot total)"),
                 sens_eff("log_pot", "Total pot biomass"), sens_eff("log_ratio", "Wheat : fava ratio"))
cmp <- log_eff %>% left_join(alt, by = c("response", "Water")) %>% filter(Water == "Control")
knitr::kable(cmp %>% transmute(response,
                               `equal variance` = sprintf("%+.0f%% [%.0f, %.0f]", pct, pct_lo, pct_hi),
                               `varIdent(~1|Inoc)` = sprintf("%+.0f%% [%.0f, %.0f]", pct_alt, lo_alt, hi_alt)),
             caption = "SENSITIVITY - Control water effects under equal variance vs. a separate variance for inoculated and sterile pots")
```

```{r save}
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(log_eff, "outputs/competitive_balance_effects_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(gram_eff, "outputs/competitive_balance_effects_grams.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 3. What the data support (EXPLORATORY)

```{r headline}
g <- function(resp, w, col) {
  x <- log_eff %>% filter(response == resp, Water == w); x[[col]]
}
pot_c <- log_eff %>% filter(response == "Total pot biomass", Water == "Control")
gr_c  <- gram_eff %>% filter(response == "Total pot biomass", Water == "Control")
```

* **Fava loses, strongly, at control and moderate water; not at severe.** −72% and −74% (CIs well clear
  of zero); at severe −3% (CI −34 to +42).
* **Wheat does not detectably gain anywhere.** Pot-total wheat changes are −9%, +15% and +8%, all with
  CIs spanning zero by a wide margin (about −36% to +63%). The data are consistent with a wheat
  gain, no change, or a loss; they cannot say wheat is better off. Wheat is the noisy component (a
  pot-level CI of roughly ±10 g).
* **Total pot productivity at control: a suggestive loss, not a demonstrated one.** The point estimate
  is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", pot_c$pct)` (95% CI `r sprintf("%.0f%% to %+.0f%%", pot_c$pct_lo, pot_c$pct_hi)`, p = `r fmt_p(pot_c$p)`), or
  `r sprintf("%.1f g", gr_c$est)` per pot (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f to %+.1f g", gr_c$lo, gr_c$hi)`, p = `r fmt_p(gr_c$p)`). The raw −20% (ratio of
  arithmetic means) corresponds to about −23% in the log-scale model, and the interval includes zero. State it as
  "the pot lost about 20% of its biomass at control, but with n = 5 this was not statistically
  distinguishable from no change". Nothing detectable at moderate (−5%) or severe (+4%) water.
* **The ratio shifts strongly toward wheat, but only because fava shrinks.** The wheat:fava ratio
  rose about 3.3-fold at control and 4.4-fold at moderate water, and not at severe. Wheat did not
  gain (above), so this is a fava effect expressed as a ratio.

**The framing in the prompt holds, with one qualification.** "Wheat does not reliably gain when fava
is suppressed" is supported. "Under adequate water the pot simply loses biomass" is the right
direction but is **not established**: the loss at control is borderline, and the missing biomass is
entirely the fava's.

# 4. Two caveats (must accompany any figure from this section)

1. **Inoculum confound.** Inoculated pots received live INVAM material (spores, hyphae, root
   fragments, carrier medium, and co-introduced microbiota); sterile pots received nothing. A
   biomass loss concentrated entirely in the legume has an obvious alternative explanation:
   something in the inoculum harmed fava directly, independent of AMF or of any competition with
   wheat. There is no killed-inoculum-plus-filtrate control to separate these. Sterile pots also
   showed background colonization (hyphal colonization up to 0.47), so the contrast is
   attenuated, not clean.
2. **AMF-rhizobia carbon competition is a hypothesis, not a finding.** Fava was nodulating, and AMF
   and rhizobia both draw photosynthate, so a tripartite symbiosis can be net costly to the
   legume. Nodulation was observed at harvest but never quantified (no counts or masses), so this
   mechanism is untested. Fava's own AMF colonization was never measured either (fava roots were
   not stained), so what is called "AMF" in the fava response is wheat's randomized inoculation
   treatment, not fava's colonization.

# 5. Figure 3 (two panels), EXPLORATORY

Two-panel replacement for the single-panel Figure 3. **Panel A** is the fava biomass figure from
`14_Figure3_FavaSuppression/fig3_redesign.R` (individual pots, model geometric mean with 95% CI,
and an anchored bracket giving the % change). **Panel B** shows the pot composition, so the change
in total productivity is visible next to which component moved. Panel B is built two ways so you
can choose: **stacked bars** (the pot as a whole) and **side-by-side components** (wheat, fava and
total on one shared axis).

Encoding follows `fig_style.R`: blue = the intercrop stand, filled = inoculated, open = sterile.
Panel B in grams uses identity-scale models (the model estimate of a difference in means equals the
raw difference, so the bars, the points and the bracket labels agree). Panel A's % changes come from
the log-scale model, as in section 2.

```{r fig-setup}
library(patchwork)
source("../fig_style.R")

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
DODGE <- 0.6                 # same geometry as fig3_redesign.R: two groups sit at x +/- DODGE/4
OFF   <- DODGE / 4
col   <- pal_poly[["Inter"]]
minus <- function(x, d = 1) gsub("-", "\u2212", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, flag = "+"), fixed = TRUE)

# ---- identity-scale cell means with 95% CI, for panel B ---------------------------------------
cell_means <- map_dfr(c(Wheat = "wheat", Fava = "fava", `Total pot` = "pot"), function(v) {
  emmeans(lm(reformulate("Inoc * Water", v), data = inter), ~ Inoc | Water) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    transmute(Water = factor(Water, levels(inter$Water)), Inoc = factor(Inoc, levels(inter$Inoc)),
              mean = emmean, lo = lower.CL, hi = upper.CL)
}, .id = "comp") %>% mutate(comp = factor(comp, c("Wheat", "Fava", "Total pot")))

# difference (Inoc - Strl) in grams, per component and water level
gram_lab <- gram_eff %>%
  mutate(comp = factor(unname(c(`Fava biomass` = "Fava", `Wheat biomass (pot total)` = "Wheat",
                                `Total pot biomass` = "Total pot")[response]), c("Wheat", "Fava", "Total pot")),
         sig = lo > 0 | hi < 0)
stopifnot(nrow(gram_lab) == 9)
```

## Panel A: fava biomass (from `fig3_redesign.R`)

```{r panel-a, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
mm_a <- emmeans(lm(log_fava ~ Inoc * Water, data = inter), ~ Inoc | Water) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(Water = factor(Water, levels(inter$Water)), Inoc = factor(Inoc, levels(inter$Inoc)),
            fit = exp(emmean), lo = exp(lower.CL), hi = exp(upper.CL))

# brackets sit above BOTH the raw pots and the top of the CI line, so nothing crosses them
brk_a <- inter %>% group_by(Water) %>% summarise(top = max(fava), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(mm_a %>% group_by(Water) %>% summarise(ci_hi = max(hi), .groups = "drop"), by = "Water") %>%
  mutate(top = pmax(top, ci_hi)) %>%
  mutate(Water = factor(Water, levels(inter$Water)), xn = as.numeric(Water),
         ybar = top * 1.12, ytick = top * 1.05, ylab_ = ybar * 1.045) %>%
  left_join(log_eff %>% filter(response == "Fava biomass") %>% select(Water, pct, pct_lo, pct_hi, p), by = "Water") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(minus(pct, 0), "%  (", minus(pct_lo, 0), " to ", minus(pct_hi, 0), ")"),
         sig = p < 0.05)

legend_inoc <- function() list(
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Inoc = 21, Strl = 21), labels = inoc_lab),
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Inoc = col, Strl = "white"), labels = inoc_lab),
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3.4, colour = col)),
         fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3.4, colour = col))))

fig_a <- ggplot(inter, aes(x = Water, y = fava)) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_a, aes(x = xn - OFF, xend = xn + OFF, y = ybar, yend = ybar),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_a, aes(x = xn - OFF, xend = xn - OFF, y = ybar, yend = ytick),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_a, aes(x = xn + OFF, xend = xn + OFF, y = ybar, yend = ytick),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = brk_a, aes(x = xn, y = ylab_, label = label, colour = sig,
                              fontface = ifelse(sig, "bold", "plain")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.3, vjust = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey15", `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Inoc), colour = col, size = 2.1, stroke = 0.9, fill = NA, alpha = 0.75,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.10, dodge.width = DODGE, seed = 1)) +
  geom_linerange(data = mm_a, aes(y = fit, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, group = Inoc), colour = col,
                 linewidth = 0.6, position = position_dodge(width = DODGE)) +
  geom_point(data = mm_a, aes(y = fit, shape = Inoc, fill = Inoc), colour = col, size = 3.4, stroke = 1.1,
             position = position_dodge(width = DODGE)) +
  legend_inoc() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = water_lab) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, 2), limits = c(0, max(brk_a$ylab_) * 1.12),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fava biomass per plant (g)",
       title = "Fava biomass",
       subtitle = "Change with inoculated vs. sterile wheat (95% CI). Large points: model mean; small points: pots.") +
  theme_ms(11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 8.8),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
print(fig_a)
```

## Panel B, layout 1: stacked bars

Each bar is the mean pot, wheat (bottom) plus fava (top), for inoculated and sterile pots at each
water level. Open circles are each pot's **total** biomass. The bracket gives the unadjusted p-value
for the difference in total pot biomass (inoculated vs. sterile); it is grey when p >= 0.05. The
size of the change and its CI are in the caption and in section 2b.

```{r panel-b-stacked, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.4, dpi=150}
stack <- cell_means %>% filter(comp %in% c("Wheat", "Fava")) %>%
  mutate(comp = factor(comp, c("Fava", "Wheat")))            # first level is stacked on top

brk_s <- inter %>% group_by(Water) %>% summarise(top = max(pot), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ybar = top + 2.2, ytick = top + 0.9, ylab_ = ybar + 0.7) %>%
  left_join(gram_lab %>% filter(comp == "Total pot") %>% select(Water, p, sig), by = "Water") %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(p < 1e-4, "p < 0.0001", paste0("p = ", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 2))))

fig_b_stacked <- ggplot(stack, aes(x = Inoc, y = mean)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = comp), colour = col, width = 0.66, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = inter, aes(x = Inoc, y = pot), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, fill = "white",
             colour = "grey25", size = 1.9, stroke = 0.8,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 2)) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_s, aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = ybar, yend = ybar), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_s, aes(x = 1, xend = 1, y = ybar, yend = ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_s, aes(x = 2, xend = 2, y = ybar, yend = ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = brk_s, aes(x = 1.5, y = ylab_, label = label, colour = sig, fontface = ifelse(sig, "bold", "plain")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1, vjust = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey15", `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Wheat = col, Fava = scales::alpha(col, 0.28)), breaks = c("Wheat", "Fava"),
                    labels = c(Wheat = "Wheat (6 plants)", Fava = "Fava (1 plant)")) +
  facet_wrap(~ Water, nrow = 1, strip.position = "bottom", labeller = labeller(Water = water_lab)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = inoc_lab) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10), limits = c(0, max(brk_s$ylab_) * 1.1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Biomass per pot (g)", title = "Pot composition",
       subtitle = "Bars: mean wheat + fava. Open circles: total biomass of each pot. Bracket: p-value for the change in total.") +
  theme_ms(11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 8.8),
        strip.placement = "outside", strip.text = element_text(face = "plain", size = 10),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.spacing.x = unit(1.4, "lines"))
print(fig_b_stacked)

fig3_stacked <- fig_a / fig_b_stacked + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.05)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", caption = "Exploratory. CIs and p-values unadjusted. n = 5 pots per group.",
                  theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", size = 8.5, hjust = 0)))
ggsave("figures/Fig3AB_Stacked.pdf", fig3_stacked, width = 7.5, height = 9.2)
ggsave("figures/Fig3AB_Stacked.png", fig3_stacked, width = 7.5, height = 9.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Panel B, layout 2: side-by-side components

Wheat, fava and total pot on **one shared axis** (grams per pot), so the size of each component's
change can be compared directly. Large points are cell means with 95% CIs, small points are pots; the
label is the difference (inoculated minus sterile) in grams, bold when its CI excludes zero.

```{r panel-b-components, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
pts_b <- inter %>% select(Water, Inoc, Wheat = wheat, Fava = fava, `Total pot` = pot) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Wheat, Fava, `Total pot`), names_to = "comp", values_to = "y") %>%
  mutate(comp = factor(comp, c("Wheat", "Fava", "Total pot")))

brk_c <- pts_b %>% group_by(comp, Water) %>% summarise(top = max(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(cell_means %>% group_by(comp, Water) %>% summarise(ci_hi = max(hi), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("comp", "Water")) %>% mutate(top = pmax(top, ci_hi)) %>%
  mutate(xn = as.numeric(Water), ybar = top + 2.2, ytick = top + 0.9, ylab_ = ybar + 0.6) %>%
  left_join(gram_lab %>% select(comp, Water, est, sig), by = c("comp", "Water")) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(minus(est, 1), " g"))

comp_lab <- c(Wheat = "Wheat (6 plants)", Fava = "Fava (1 plant)", `Total pot` = "Total pot")
water_short <- c(Control = "Control\n80% FC", Moderate = "Moderate\n60% FC", Severe = "Severe\n40% FC")

fig_b_comp <- ggplot(pts_b, aes(x = Water, y = y)) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_c, aes(x = xn - OFF, xend = xn + OFF, y = ybar, yend = ybar), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_c, aes(x = xn - OFF, xend = xn - OFF, y = ybar, yend = ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(data = brk_c, aes(x = xn + OFF, xend = xn + OFF, y = ybar, yend = ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = brk_c, aes(x = xn, y = ylab_, label = label, colour = sig, fontface = ifelse(sig, "bold", "plain")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.9, vjust = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey15", `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Inoc), colour = col, size = 1.6, stroke = 0.8, fill = NA, alpha = 0.7,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.10, dodge.width = DODGE, seed = 1)) +
  geom_linerange(data = cell_means, aes(y = mean, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, group = Inoc), colour = col,
                 linewidth = 0.55, position = position_dodge(width = DODGE)) +
  geom_point(data = cell_means, aes(y = mean, shape = Inoc, fill = Inoc), colour = col, size = 2.8, stroke = 1,
             position = position_dodge(width = DODGE)) +
  legend_inoc() +
  facet_wrap(~ comp, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(comp = comp_lab)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = water_short) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10), limits = c(0, max(brk_c$ylab_) * 1.1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Biomass per pot (g)", title = "Pot composition",
       subtitle = "Same axis in every panel. Labels: change with inoculation (g); bold if the 95% CI excludes zero.") +
  theme_ms(11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 8.8),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.9), panel.spacing.x = unit(1, "lines"))
print(fig_b_comp)

fig3_components <- (fig_a + theme(legend.position = "none")) / fig_b_comp + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", caption = "Exploratory. CIs and p-values unadjusted. n = 5 pots per group.",
                  theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", size = 8.5, hjust = 0)))
ggsave("figures/Fig3AB_Components.pdf", fig3_components, width = 7.5, height = 8.6)
ggsave("figures/Fig3AB_Components.png", fig3_components, width = 7.5, height = 8.6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Proposed caption (either layout)

> **Figure 3. Inoculated wheat suppressed its fava neighbor under adequate water, but the pot's
> total biomass did not change detectably (exploratory).** (A) Fava biomass per plant (one fava per
> pot) in the 30 wheat/ fava intercrop pots, by wheat inoculation (filled = inoculated, open =
> sterile) and water level (FC = field capacity). Small points are pots; large points are model
> geometric means with 95% CIs; brackets give the change in fava biomass with inoculated wheat (95%
> CI). (B) Pot composition: wheat (6 plants) and fava biomass per pot. Inoculation reduced fava
> biomass by about 6 g per pot at control and moderate water; wheat biomass per pot did not change
> detectably at any water level (95% CIs span roughly -11 to +15 g), so total pot biomass fell by
> `r minus(gr_c$est, 1)` g (95% CI `r minus(gr_c$lo, 1)` to `r minus(gr_c$hi, 1)`) at control water, an interval that includes zero.
> Brackets in B give the unadjusted p-value for the difference in total pot biomass. n = 5 pots per group; all CIs and p-values are unadjusted. The inoculated pots received live inoculum with
> co-introduced microbiota and the sterile pots received nothing, so a direct effect of the inoculum
> on fava cannot be separated from an AMF effect (no killed-inoculum control).

## Notes for the Results text

* **Say what the data support.** Fava lost about 6 g per pot at control and moderate water, with
  tight CIs. Wheat showed no detectable change at any level, but its pot-level uncertainty is
  large (about ±10 g), so "wheat did not gain" is "no detectable gain", not "no gain".
* **Do not call the total-pot loss a finding.** At control the pot lost about 20% of its biomass
  (-7.5 g), 95% CI -17.0 to +2.0 g. It is suggestive, not established.
* **The ratio and the fava share are fava effects.** The wheat:fava ratio shifting toward wheat (3.3x
  and 4.4x) does not mean wheat gained; it is the fava loss expressed as a ratio.
* **Keep the two caveats attached** to any use of this figure: the inoculum confound, and the
  AMF-rhizobia carbon competition as an untested hypothesis (nodulation was observed, never quantified).
* **Units differ by panel on purpose.** Panel A's % changes come from the log-scale fava model; panel
  B is in grams from identity-scale models, so bars, points and labels agree and the wheat and fava
  changes add to the total. Panel A's large points are geometric means and panel B's are arithmetic
  means, so the fava values differ slightly between the panels (for example 8.4 vs 8.5 g at control).
